# @gears-frontx/telemetry

> Browser telemetry SDK for FrontX. Batches app events and POSTs them to an endpoint you control. Session tracking, device/navigation context, DOM autocapture, plugin system.

Ecosystem package (`packages/telemetry`), standalone by construction: no intra-ecosystem `@gears-frontx` imports, no React, no deep `@gears-frontx/*/src/**` imports - enforced for every file under `packages/telemetry` by the root `eslint.config.js`, plus `frontx-telemetry-1-no-template-content` and `frontx-single-intra-ecosystem-edge-telemetry-standalone` in `.dependency-cruiser.cjs`. One runtime dependency: `bowser` 2.11.0, used only in `src/plugins/device.ts` for OS name/version, browser name/version and platform type; everything else is native DOM. Browser-only: needs `window`, `document`, `localStorage`, `fetch`, `crypto.randomUUID`, `Intl.Locale`.

## Entry Point

Exactly one: `.` (`@gears-frontx/telemetry`). No subpath exports. Wiring this SDK into a FrontX app is template-side work - the framework lives at `template-standard/packages/framework` and `packages/cyber-pilot-kit-frontx/guidelines/ecosystem-boundaries.md:28-31` forbids an ecosystem package importing template territory at the source level - so no framework-plugin API ships from here.

## Core API

- [createTelemetry](src/services/telemetry.ts): `(config: TelemetryConfig) => TelemetryService` - build a client; no listeners and no plugin `setup` until `start()`, though `logEvent` already queues and flushes
- [telemetryLocalePlugin](src/plugins/locale.ts): `(source: LocaleSource) => { name: 'locale', setup }` - a telemetry plugin (the plugin type itself is internal, not an export) that sets `context_language` per event, maximized to BCP 47 (`en` -> `en-US`)
- [telemetryElementHookKey](src/plugins/autocapture/elementHook.ts): `unique symbol` = `Symbol.for('@gears-frontx/telemetry/element-hook')` - the element property autocapture reads a hook from; augments global `Element`

## TelemetryService

| Method | Returns | Notes |
|--------|---------|-------|
| `start()` | `TelemetryService` | Registers built-in plugins, runs every plugin `setup`, starts session tracking and the flush scheduler, fires `start` hooks |
| `logEvent(name, data?)` | `void` | Also accepts one full record: `logEvent({ name, data, ...context })`. `id` and `time_triggered` are set after caller fields, so a caller cannot forge them |
| `identify(id)` | `TelemetryService` | `string \| number`; sets `context_user_id` on later events only |
| `plugin(...plugins)` | `TelemetryService` | Falsy entries ignored, so `cond && myPlugin()` is safe |
| `destroy()` | `void` | Removes listeners, cancels the scheduler, fires `destroy` hooks |

Chainable except `logEvent` and `destroy`. `start()`, `plugin()` and `destroy()` no-op when `window` is undefined (SSR); `logEvent()` and `identify()` do not.

Plugins are keyed by `name` (same name replaces) and are set up once, inside `start()` -> call `plugin()` before `start()` or the plugin never runs. Built-ins are registered inside `start()`, after your plugins, so their `event` hooks run last and overwrite: device/OS/client/timezone fields (`device.ts`), `context_app_*` and `context_call_chain` (`appInfo.ts`).

`destroy()` does not flush - queued events are dropped.

## Config

`TelemetryConfig`, normalized by [normalizeOptions](src/utils/utils.ts):

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
|-------|------|---------|-------|
| `appName` | `string` | required | `context_source_app_name`; default for `context_app_name` and `context_service_name` |
| `appVersion` | `string` | required | `context_source_app_version` |
| `url` | `string` | `/api/events` | apiVersion 1 -> `/api/events`, else `/api/telemetry/v{apiVersion}/events` |
| `autocapture` | `boolean` | `true` | DOM `click`/`change`/`submit` capture |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `false` still collects, enriches and drains the queue - only the POST is skipped |
| `verbose` | `boolean` | `false` | Console logging from the SDK's logger |
| `storagePrefix` | `string` | none | Infix in the owned keys: `telemetry_{prefix}_device_id`, `telemetry_{prefix}_session` |
| `sessionDuration` | `number` | `1800000` | Inactivity window (ms) before a stored session is treated as ended |
| `apiVersion` | `number` | `1` | Wire envelope, see Transport |

## Quick Start

```typescript
import { createTelemetry, telemetryLocalePlugin } from '@gears-frontx/telemetry';

const telemetry = createTelemetry({
  appName: 'my-app',
  appVersion: '1.4.2',
  url: 'https://telemetry.example.com/api/events',
})
  .plugin(telemetryLocalePlugin(i18next))
  .plugin({
    name: 'tenant',
    setup: (context) => {
      context.addHook('event', (record) => {
        record.context_tenant_id = tenantId;
      });
    },
  });

telemetry.identify(user.id);
telemetry.start();
telemetry.logEvent('settings_saved', { theme: 'dark' });
```

## Emitted Events

- `session_start` - on `start()` when no live session is in `localStorage`
- `page_view` - `data.url` = pathname; on `popstate` and on patched `history.pushState`/`replaceState`, deduped per pathname. `start()` alone emits none. Later events carry `caused_by_id` = the current page_view id
- `autocapture_click` / `autocapture_change` / `autocapture_submit`

Session activity is refreshed on `scroll`/`keydown`/`click` (debounced 100ms) and on every `page_view`.

## Transport

`logEvent -> event hooks -> queue -> flush`. The timer restarts on every event, so a flush lands 5s after the last one; `visibilitychange` to `hidden` flushes immediately. `fetch` is `keepalive` with fixed `Content-Type: application/vnd.kafka.json.v2+json` and Kafka `Accept` headers (not configurable), and a rejected POST goes to `console.error`, never retried. Each record gains `time_sent` at flush.

- apiVersion 1 -> `{ records: [{ key: id, value: record }] }`. Every nested object is stringified field-by-field, so `data: { a: 'b' }` arrives as `data: { a: '"b"' }`.
- apiVersion 2 -> `{ meta, records }`; `context_user_id` and `context_tenant_id` are deleted, and fields identical across a batch of 2+ are hoisted into `meta`. A single-record batch leaves `meta` empty.

## Autocapture

Capture-phase passive listeners on `document` for `click`, `change`, `submit`. The walk goes from the event target up to `body` (crossing shadow boundaries via `host`); only `a`, `button`, `form`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `label` produce the base record, and `$el_text` only comes from `a`, `button`, `label` (capped at 1000 chars). Autocapture owns the `$` prefix in `data`: `$el_tag_name`, `$el_text`, `$el_attr_*` (incl. `$el_attr_class` from `classList`, `$el_attr_href`), `$external_click_url`. `style`, `fill`, `viewBox`, `xmlns` and `data-telemetry-no-capture` are never captured as attributes.

Redaction: a `hidden`/`password` input, or an element whose `name` or `id` looks sensitive (`cvv`, `ssn`, `cardnum`, `pwd`, `routing`, ...), anywhere on the walked path suppresses the whole event; values shaped like a credit card or US SSN are dropped; on `select`, `textarea`, `contenteditable="true"` and any `input` whose type is not `button`/`checkbox`/`submit`/`reset`, only `name`, `id`, `aria-label` are read. Safety net, not a compliance guarantee.

Opt out per subtree with `data-telemetry-no-capture="false"`. The value is inverted: a bare attribute or `="true"` does nothing.

## Element Hooks

```typescript
import { telemetryElementHookKey } from '@gears-frontx/telemetry';

el[telemetryElementHookKey] = () => ({
  context: {
    context_service_name: 'settings-panel',
    context_service_version: '1.0.0',
    context_call_chain: ['settings-panel'],
  },
  data: { section: 'appearance' },
});
```

- Allowlist: only `context_service_name`, `context_service_version`, `context_call_chain` survive a hook. Anything else is dropped - other record fields are overwritten by built-in plugins before send.
- `{ capture: false }` from any hook on the path suppresses the whole event; `context`/`data` in the same return are then ignored.
- The closest hook returning a usable contribution wins its whole field set. `context` from one hook is never mixed with `data` from another, and a field the winning hook left out (or set to an explicit `undefined`) stays unset - no farther-out hook fills the gap. A non-object `context` or `data` counts as no contribution.
- `data` merges underneath autocapture's own keys; hook keys starting with `$` are stripped.
- `context_call_chain` must be the registering element's complete chain. `appInfo` prepends `appName` and warns when the chain lacks the service name; chains are never stitched across hooks.
- A throwing hook degrades that element to no contribution; the event is still emitted, and the first thrown value is rethrown out of the listener afterwards (wrapped in an `Error` with `cause` when it is not an `Error`) so it reaches `window.onerror`.
- Cross-deployment contract (reader and writers can be on different versions): evolve additively; a semantic change needs a new registry-symbol string, not a new meaning for this one.

## Writing a Plugin

`{ name: string, setup: (context) => void }`. `context` carries `config` (normalized), `addHook`, `logEvent` (returns the record), `getSession`, `refreshSession`, `logger`. Hook keys: `event` (mutate the record before it is queued), `start`, `destroy`. `sessionStart` is declared in `TelemetryHooks` but never called. Hooks of one key all run even if one throws; the first error is rethrown after the last hook.

## Types

```typescript
import type {
  TelemetryService,                  // client returned by createTelemetry
  TelemetryLogEvent,                 // (...args: TelemetryLogEventParams) => void
  TelemetryLogEventParams,           // [name, data?] | [record]
  TelemetryEventRecord,              // name, data, and the context_* fields
  TelemetryData,                     // Record<string, unknown>
  TelemetryConfig,                   // see Config
  LocaleSource,                      // { language: string }, read per event
  TelemetryElementHook,              // () => TelemetryElementHookResult
  TelemetryElementHookResult,        // { capture?: false; context?; data? } | void
  TelemetryElementHookAttribution,   // the three hook-settable context_* fields
} from '@gears-frontx/telemetry';
```

Several declared `TelemetryEventRecord` fields are never populated by the SDK (`context_user_email`, `context_tenant_id`, `context_device_screen_*`, `context_session_duration`, `context_dom_element_*`, ...); a plugin or a `logEvent` record has to set them.
